extracted: wave-7 opener, 2026-09-27, from scenario/upstream-test-harness.js (+ upstream-harness-matchers.js, upstream-harness-vi.js, upstream-fake-timers.js) and upstream/shims/{expect-async-chain,expect-poll,vi-wait,describe-each}.js — the committed vitest subset the transpiled specs import as `vitest` (test/upstream-suite/transpile.mjs maps the specifier to scenario/upstream-test-harness.js)
unimplementedPolicy: APIs outside this subset fail LOUD naming the API (rule 5). vi.mock is the documented exclusion: 'loader-level interception — the transpiler excludes specs that need it'.

matchers.name: toBe
matchers.semantics: Object.is identity (incl. NaN).

matchers.name: toEqual
matchers.semantics: Strict subset match (matchSubset strict=true): keys whose value is undefined ignored on BOTH sides (vitest's equals: {a:1} equals {a:1, nested:undefined}); asymmetric matchers (__matcher face of expect.objectContaining & co) honored; BOTH-sides-Errors compare by name+message (quickjs owns stack as ENUMERABLE, so the generic own-key walk failed toEqual(new Error(m)) on key count alone); an Error ACTUAL under non-strict walks the name/message face plus own extras; non-strict (toMatchObject) reads through PROPERTY ACCESS so prototype getters match; arrays: expected may be a prefix subset (non-strict) or equal-length (strict).

matchers.name: toStrictEqual
matchers.semantics: deepEqual (no undefined-key tolerance; keeps the {a:1} vs {a:1,nested:undefined} distinction); Set equality is MEMBERSHIP not insertion order (measured 2026-09-23); Date by time, Error by message, Map by entries; depth cap 64.

matchers.name: toMatchObject
matchers.semantics: Non-strict subset match (matchSubset strict=false): property-ACCESS reads (prototype getters match — fetch-values Response/Request faces); Error actuals judged by name/message face plus own extras.

matchers.name: toContain
matchers.semantics: Arrays use SAME-VALUE membership (identity — deep equality would find any structurally-equal member; measured on the deque release test); strings substring; Sets .has(); asymmetric matchers still apply per element.

matchers.name: toContainEqual
matchers.semantics: matchSubset (not deepEqual) per element — the corpus passes asymmetric matchers nested inside rows.

matchers.name: toHaveLength
matchers.semantics: actual?.length === n.

matchers.name: toMatch
matchers.semantics: String subject: RegExp test or substring inclusion.

matchers.name: toMatchInlineSnapshot
matchers.semantics: Inline snapshot without a disk: the stored template is dedented (leading newline dropped, common indentation stripped, trailing blank lines trimmed) and a string actual serializes quoted with real newlines kept (terminal tools PTC output-map projection is the only corpus user).

matchers.name: toMatchFileSnapshot
matchers.semantics: File-snapshot without a disk: the store lives on the global (one spec per runtime), writes on FIRST sight and compares on repeats (per-run stability asserted; CI-strict compare-every-run is not reproducible — the transpiler seeds no expected/ files and the runtime keeps no persistent disk).

matchers.name: toBeCloseTo
matchers.semantics: |actual - n| < 10^-precision / 2 (precision default 2).

matchers.name: toBeGreaterThan
matchers.semantics: actual > n.

matchers.name: toBeGreaterThanOrEqual
matchers.semantics: actual >= n.

matchers.name: toBeLessThan
matchers.semantics: actual < n.

matchers.name: toBeLessThanOrEqual
matchers.semantics: actual <= n.

matchers.name: toBeInstanceOf
matchers.semantics: instanceof, plus the vendoring-parity arm (W6-V): a same-named Error pair across the staged-src-bundle vs published-lib copy boundary passes — narrow on purpose (fires only when instanceof failed, both sides Error, constructor names agree modulo esbuild's `_` dedupe prefix and trailing digits).

matchers.name: toBeNull
matchers.semantics: actual === null.

matchers.name: toBeUndefined
matchers.semantics: actual === undefined.

matchers.name: toBeDefined
matchers.semantics: actual !== undefined.

matchers.name: toBeTruthy
matchers.semantics: Boolean(actual).

matchers.name: toBeFalsy
matchers.semantics: !Boolean(actual).

matchers.name: toBeNaN
matchers.semantics: Number.isNaN.

matchers.name: toBeTypeOf
matchers.semantics: typeof with null spelled 'null'; expected 'function' accepts any function.

matchers.name: toHaveProperty
matchers.semantics: Dot-path (or key array) walk through PROPERTY ACCESS (class methods on the PROTOTYPE match — createTransport table, W4-M); absent = undefined AND no own key; with a value argument the terminal value deep-equals; without one, existence only.

matchers.name: toThrow
matchers.semantics: A DID-THROW flag (throw undefined still counts — the resolves/rejects settle wrapper throws undefined for settled-undefined values). Expected forms: string (message contains), RegExp (message matches, the got-message echo stays in the verdict so it.each drift is diagnosable), Error instance (compared by MESSAGE and identity — jest's contract, measured 2026-09-28), asymmetric matcher (invoked over the WHOLE thrown error before any equality), plain object (subset match; verdict echoes name+message+code — W7-Y1), constructor class (instanceof).

matchers.name: toThrowError
matchers.semantics: vitest alias of toThrow.

matchers.name: toSatisfy
matchers.semantics: predicate(actual) truthy.

matchers.name: toHaveBeenCalled
matchers.semantics: mock.calls.length > 0.

matchers.name: toHaveBeenCalledOnce
matchers.semantics: mock.calls.length === 1.

matchers.name: toHaveBeenCalledTimes
matchers.semantics: mock.calls.length === n.

matchers.name: toHaveBeenCalledWith
matchers.semantics: Some call with matching arity and per-arg non-strict subset match (asymmetric matchers honored).

matchers.name: toHaveBeenNthCalledWith
matchers.semantics: Call #n (1-based) with the expected args (same matching as toHaveBeenCalledWith).

matchers.name: toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith
matchers.semantics: Exactly-once + args compound (tool-subagent-control interrupt suite asserts the child's cancel call).

matchers.name: toHaveBeenLastCalledWith
matchers.semantics: The last call with the expected args (alias: toHaveBeenCalledLastWith).

matchers.name: resolves
matchers.semantics: Chain head: unwraps a FUNCTION subject by calling it before awaiting (vitest: `typeof obj === 'function' ? obj() : obj` — the corpus's dominant form); the settled matcher then applies; .not negates the SETTLED matcher; toThrow on a resolved promise fails (not.toThrow passes) regardless of the resolved value.

matchers.name: rejects
matchers.semantics: Chain head: the subject must reject (a resolution fails with 'expected the promise to reject, but it resolved'); the THROWN error feeds the matcher (toThrow arms included); the custom failure MESSAGE threads through (W4-N).

matchers.name: not
matchers.semantics: LAZY negation (eager construction would recurse forever); the custom failure MESSAGE rides along (vitest's expect(x, msg).not.toContain() throws with msg as the failure text).

matchers.name: poll
matchers.semantics: expect.poll(getter, {interval=50, timeout=5000}) — awaits the getter until the chained matcher passes; paces the real event loop via the 0-delay timer arm; 5s default (vitest's 1s times out on a loaded box, measured).

expectStatic.name: extend
expectStatic.semantics: Loud failure: 'harness: expect.extend is not implemented'.

expectStatic.name: soft
expectStatic.semantics: Records-and-continues in vitest; here soft asserts FAIL IMMEDIATELY — the verdict is identical, only later assertions in the same test don't run (no end-of-test collector).

expectStatic.name: any
expectStatic.semantics: Asymmetric matcher: typeof by class name or instanceof.

expectStatic.name: objectContaining
expectStatic.semantics: Asymmetric matcher: non-strict subset match (matchSubset strict=false).

expectStatic.name: arrayContaining
expectStatic.semantics: Asymmetric matcher: every shape element matched by some actual element (subset per element).

expectStatic.name: expectTypeOf
expectStatic.semantics: A self-returning type-chain Proxy — any property chain composes and asserts as no-op (type-only usage).

expectStatic.name: expect(actual, message)
expectStatic.semantics: The second parameter is vitest's optional custom failure MESSAGE — a string here is a failure PREFIX; the boolean stays the internal negation flag (treating a string as negation inverted every two-arg expect — measured).

vi.name: fn
vi.semantics: A REGULAR function (not arrow) so spyOn-wrapped originals see the call-site receiver — vitest's spy forwards `this` (system-prompt-admission spies adapter.resolveModel whose body reads this.reasoning; an arrow spy broke every request, measured 2026-09-23). Ledgers: mock.calls (args array), mock.instances (the receiver per call), mock.results ({type:'return'|'throw', value}), mock.invocationCallOrder (process-wide sequence). mockImplementation / mockImplementationOnce (one-shot queue consumed before the standing impl) / mockReturnValue(Once) / mockResolvedValue(Once) / mockRejectedValue(Once).

vi.name: fn().mockClear
vi.semantics: Clears the CALL LEDGERS only — queued one-shot overrides SURVIVE it ('keeps queued overrides on mockClear').

vi.name: fn().mockReset
vi.semantics: Clears ledgers AND queued overrides AND restores the CREATION implementation ('restores the live default rule on mockReset' — remote-mock's fn was created around its default-rule dispatcher).

vi.name: spyOn
vi.semantics: Wraps object[key] with vi.fn(original); spy.mockRestore puts the original back; spies are REGISTRY-tracked for restoreAllMocks (W6-V: the 'falls back to the public decoder' test mocks the PRIVATE create static to undefined and relies on afterEach's restoreAllMocks — the old no-op left it mocked forever).

vi.name: isMockFunction
vi.semantics: typeof function && .mock !== undefined.

vi.name: stubGlobal
vi.semantics: Installs through defineProperty and restores the original PROPERTY DESCRIPTOR — not read-then-assign: a stubbed global may be (or become) a getter-only accessor (recovery.client's throwing localStorage getter) where a value read throws at stub time; returns a {mockRestore} record.

vi.name: unstubAllGlobals
vi.semantics: Calls each record's mockRestore METHOD (calling the record itself broke every stubbing spec — measured 2026-09-27).

vi.name: stubEnv
vi.semantics: Sets process.env[name]; the pre-stub value is remembered once.

vi.name: unstubAllEnvs
vi.semantics: Restores every stubbed env value (deleting entries that were absent).

vi.name: restoreAllMocks
vi.semantics: Restores every vi.spyOn spy via its mockRestore; plain vi.fn mocks stay as created (they have no original to put back — matches vitest).

vi.name: clearAllMocks
vi.semantics: No-op: spies clear on their own handles.

vi.name: mocked
vi.semantics: Identity (typing-only in vitest).

vi.name: hoisted
vi.semantics: Invokes the factory immediately (vi.hoisted(fn) -> fn()).

vi.name: mock
vi.semantics: UNIMPLEMENTED BY DESIGN: fails loud 'vi.mock is not implemented (loader-level interception) — the transpiler excludes specs that need it'.

vi.name: waitFor
vi.semantics: Retries the callback while it throws, resolves with its value; interval 50ms / timeout 5000ms defaults; rides the 0-delay timer arm on the v1.4.0 seam (resume.spec's close-swallow races synchronize on it).

vi.name: waitUntil
vi.semantics: Polls until the callback's value is truthy; same interval/timeout defaults and seam.

vi.name: useFakeTimers
vi.semantics: Swaps the AMBIENT setTimeout/clearTimeout (installed by upstream/shims/timers.js over the gateway seam) for a controlled queue the spec advances by hand; deterministic timing without the host wall clock. Also swaps the performance face (toFake:['performance']): fake now = clock.now (R3-D — deadline loops computing due = performance.now() + delay never converge against a real clock); the swap happens on EVERY install because useRealTimers restores the real object (a once-only guard left tests 2..N on wall time, measured 2026-09-27); the fake performance face is a PLAIN copy with now swapped (the perf-hooks shim freezes its object and a Proxy over it violates quickjs invariant checks). Fake timers handle the node Timeout face (ref/unref/hasRef/refresh — retention loop calls timer.unref()).

vi.name: useRealTimers
vi.semantics: Restores the real setTimeout/clearTimeout/performance; wall-clock mocking (vi.setSystemTime) stays EXCLUDED — the seam is monotonic-only.

vi.name: isFakeTimers
vi.semantics: True while the controlled queue is installed.

vi.name: advanceTimersByTime
vi.semantics: Fires every queued timer with at <= now+ms in order, moving the clock to each fire; timers armed by a fired callback inside the window fire in the same advance. Throws without useFakeTimers.

vi.name: advanceTimersByTimeAsync
vi.semantics: The ASYNC advance: fires due timers while DRAINING THE MICROTASK QUEUE between fires — the drain rides a REAL macrotask boundary (the pre-install setTimeout on the v1.4.0 gateway seam), NOT a fixed microtask unroll: the host job loop drains the ENTIRE microtask queue before a real 0ms timer fires, while a 16-tick unroll falls arbitrarily short (R3-H: the timeout-policy deadline chain armed its 100ms timer on tick ~40 and never fired). Settles the chains pending AT CALL TIME before firing due timers (a deadline armed through async middleware lands only after a real seam hop).

vi.name: runAllTimers
vi.semantics: Drains the whole queue synchronously; diverges loud at 100k fires.

vi.name: runAllTimersAsync
vi.semantics: Drains the queue letting callbacks' promise chains settle between fires (llm-retry's backoff ladder awaits this shape); same real-macrotask drain boundary as advanceTimersByTimeAsync; diverges loud at 100k fires.

vi.name: runOnlyPendingTimers
vi.semantics: Fires the currently queued timers once (clock jumps to each handle's at); no-op without fake timers.

vi.name: getTimerCount
vi.semantics: The fake queue length (0 when real).

describe.since: wave-1 (HEAD definition; see the working-tree note)
describe.semantics: Pushes name onto the current describe chain (full name = chain joined ' > '); the factory runs at collection.
The middle options argument is optional/accepted (remote-mock proxy-types spec passes {timeout}).
No-op at collection (counted at transpile time).
Runs as a plain describe (no isolation).
Runs SEQUENTIALLY — the runtime is single-threaded serial (D2); the face exists because the acp-snapshot suite selects it for replay mode (W5-T).
One describe per row; titles interpolate printf verbs positionally and $key/${key} against object rows, suffixed with the raw row for uniqueness.
pick collection vs describe.skip per a runtime condition.

it.semantics: Collects a test under the current describe chain; hooks snapshot (the beforeEach/afterEach list at collection time) is captured per test.

vitest's per-test budget spelling — the options object's timeout lands as the test record's timeoutMs (the runner's deadline default stays 5000 when absent); the process-exit spec's it.each rows pass it.
skip = no-op; only = alias of it (no isolation).

One test per row; array rows SPREAD into the callback as positional args (vitest semantics — acp codec's it.each([[reason, expected]]) destructures both), EXCEPT the degenerate EMPTY array row which arrives as the single value itself (core session canonical-envelopes seeds it.each([null, [], 1, 'invalid']) and expects [] as the row value); non-array rows pass as the single argument; titles drop leftover ${expr} and carry the raw row suffix.

vitest's it.for: a cases table collected once, each case runs the test fn as (caseValue, ctx) — ctx carries a test-scoped onTestFinished whose cleanup runs in a finally (a cleanup failure must not mask the test's own verdict); titles substitute %s and carry the value suffix.

it.since: wave-vendor (measured 2026-09-23: resume.spec's platform-gated tests call it.skipIf — an absent member is a collection-time 'not a function')
it.semantics: pick collection vs it.skip per condition.

hooks.name: beforeAll
hooks.semantics: Suite-level setup, run in order by runCollected; a throw rejects with a NAMED error ('beforeAll hook failed: ...' — the hook's identity and the thrown value are named, never silently re-thrown; bare null rejections spell 'null (rejection with null)').

hooks.name: afterAll
hooks.semantics: Suite-level teardown; vitest counts an afterAll failure as a SUITE error, not a test failure — surfaced as its own failure row AND a named rejection so the scenario verdict carries the hook's name instead of 'null' (the otel egress afterAll rejected with null and escaped unattributed before this).

hooks.name: beforeEach
hooks.semantics: Snapshotted into each test record at collection; awaited before the test fn.

hooks.name: afterEach
hooks.semantics: Awaited after the test fn in a finally; their failures NEVER mask the test's own verdict.

hooks.name: onTestFinished
hooks.semantics: Registers cleanup for the CURRENTLY-RUNNING test (or the collection tail when called at module scope — the spec's intent is teardown-after-test either way).

testContext.name: ctx.skip(note)
testContext.semantics: Raises a marker the runner classifies as 'skipped' (vitest never counts a context-skip as a failure).

testContext.name: ctx.task
testContext.semantics: The running test's handle: task.name, task.timeout (the test's time budget in ms — specs pass it as a DEADLINE value: waitForFile(marker, task.timeout, signal)); budget re-arming stays on TestRunner.getCurrentTest().timeout(ms).

testContext.name: ctx.signal
testContext.semantics: An AbortController's signal that aborts when the test finishes; tests thread it into deadline helpers and call signal.throwIfAborted() mid-body.

runner.name: TestRunner.getCurrentTest()
runner.semantics: The corpus specs ask the runner for the test they are INSIDE (`TestRunner.getCurrentTest().timeout(ms)` re-arms that test's budget — recorded on the test record and surfaced through the sink, since the runtime has no wall-clock seam to enforce a budget). Outside a run, the CURRENT test is the last one collected (module-scope callers' intent); with neither, loud failure.

runner.name: runCollected(sink)
runner.semantics: Runs everything the imported specs collected; per test: 'start' to the sink BEFORE it runs (a never-settling test — the suite's hang class, no timer seam to cut it — names the exact test a hang froze on), then beforeEach hooks, the test fn with its context (a fresh AbortController aborted in finally), pass/skip/fail classification into {passed, failed, skipped, failures}, afterEach in finally. A test fn that is not a function counts as skipped.

runner.name: resetCollection()
runner.semantics: Clears tests/suite hooks/describe chain (the driver runs one spec module per runtime).

forms: it.each table-spread (array rows spread positionally; empty-array row passes itself; non-array rows single arg)
(name, {timeout}, fn) — the middle-options collection form on it and describe
expect(actual, message) — string second arg = failure prefix, NOT negation
expect(fn).resolves / .rejects — function subjects are CALLED before awaiting
test-fn context argument: ({ skip, task, signal }) destructuring is supported (stream-rebind broke without it)
it.for(table)(name, fn) — (caseValue, ctx) shape with onTestFinished cleanup
describe.concurrent — sequential face of a parallel form (D2)
module-scope onTestFinished — attaches to the last collected test
